name: IM-1 Odysseus
objective: Demonstrate commercial lunar delivery and operate NASA science and technology payloads.
payloads: SCALPSS (Stereo Cameras for Lunar Plume-Surface Studies)
description: Intuitive Machines' Nova-C lander reached Malapert A crater rim on Feb 22, 2024, delivering 6 NASA payloads and validating commercial lunar delivery architecture.
scheduleNote: Historical landing date; completed does not mean all objectives were achieved.

name: IM-2 Athena (PRIME-1)
objective: Demonstrate lunar drilling and volatile measurement technologies with PRIME-1.
description: Athena landed in the Mons Mouton region on March 6, 2025. Its orientation limited operations; PRIME-1 demonstrated instrument functions but did not complete the planned subsurface drilling campaign.
scheduleNote: Operations concluded; this status does not imply full mission success.

name: Blue Ghost Mission 1
objective: Study lunar regolith thermal properties, cosmic radiation exposure, and solar wind interactions.
description: Blue Ghost landed in Mare Crisium on March 2, 2025, delivered ten NASA instruments, and concluded surface operations March 16.
scheduleNote: Historical landing date; surface operations ended March 16, 2025.

name: Griffin Mission 1
objective: Deliver cargo and the Astrolab FLIP rover to mature lunar mobility technology.
payloads: Astrolab FLIP (FLEX Lunar Innovation Platform) rover
description: Griffin-1 targets the Nobile Crater region and will carry the FLIP rover. The listed payload is a verified highlight, not a complete manifest.
scheduleNote: Future dates are targets and may change.

name: IM-3 (Reiner Gamma)
objective: Investigate the mysterious lunar magnetic anomaly and lunar swirl formation.
description: Dispatches a cooperative team of autonomous rovers (CADRE) and magnetometers to study the enigmatic mini-magnetosphere of Reiner Gamma.
scheduleNote: Future dates are targets and may change.

name: Artemis II
landingArea: Crewed lunar flyby; no lunar landing
objective: Test crewed Orion operations and deep-space systems during a lunar flyby.
payloads: Crew of 4 Astronauts (Wiseman, Glover, Koch, Hansen)
description: Four astronauts flew around the Moon and returned to Earth in April 2026. This mission had no lunar surface destination.
scheduleNote: Historical mission dates; no lunar landing.

name: Artemis III
lander: Orion and commercial HLS test articles
landingArea: Low Earth orbit; no lunar landing
objective: Demonstrate rendezvous and docking operations with commercial human landing system test articles in Earth orbit.
payloads: Commercial human landing system test articles
description: The current Artemis III plan is an Earth-orbit demonstration with Orion and commercial lander test articles. It is not a lunar surface landing mission.
scheduleNote: Future dates are targets and may change.

name: Draper CP-12 (former APEX 1.0)
objective: Former plan: deliver geophysical instruments to the lunar far side.
payloads: LITMS (planned Lunar Interior Temperature and Materials Suite)
description: Draper and NASA mutually ended CLPS task order CP-12 in July 2026, according to ispace-U.S. The former Schrödinger Basin destination is retained only as historical context.
scheduleNote: Cancelled task order; no scheduled landing or active destination.
